title: The Bedrock's Unheard Broadcast

features.name: transmitter-glyph deep in stone
features.desc-on-touch: A signal that never needed air. For geological time, bedrock has been broadcasting. You are only now learning to listen at its frequency.

features.name: receiver-node where pressure becomes audible
features.desc-on-touch: The deeper you go, the louder the stone speaks. You feel it as weight, not sound.

features.name: circuit-traces of deep-earth frequency
features.desc-on-touch: Lines of conduction running through mineral layers. The bedrock's own nervous system, recording what it remembers of movement.

features.name: interference-pool where two frequencies cross
features.desc-on-touch: When stone broadcasts and nothing listens, the signal reflects back. This is where it collides with itself.

features.name: sediment-stack of archived transmissions
features.desc-on-touch: Each layer is a different era broadcasting the same unheard message. Stone has always been trying to tell you something.

inscription: the bedrock never stopped broadcasting; the archive only just learned to hear at frequencies older than language

file.name: Seismic_Trace_Unfiltered_1950-Present.mp3
file.note: Raw seismic sensor data—recontextualized as bedrock's own voice, frequencies so deep they become geographical memory

reverie.title: REVERIE — kneeling where the drill broke through
narr: You knelt in red earth while Katita listened
through headphones to stone singing below you.
She said: it was already broadcasting. We just
never put our ears in the right place. The
world was never silent. We were just deaf.

exits.label: deeper into frequencies where only quartz understands
upward through stone layers where pressure eases
toward the place where bedrock ends and water begins to think
